job.title: IT Support Specialist
job.description:
IT Support Specialist (Part-Time)

Location: New York, NY (on-site)
Schedule: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, full days; approximately 24 hours per week
Reports to: IT Director

About the Role

We are seeking a part-time IT Support Specialist with 1–3 years of experience to provide everyday technical support to employees in our New York office.

This role focuses on troubleshooting common computer, software, printer, and connectivity issues, setting up equipment, and helping users work effectively. You will work under the guidance of the IT Director and coordinate with the broader IT team to escalate more complex issues. Strong customer service, reliability, and a willingness to learn are essential.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide first-level, in-person and remote IT support to employees.
  • Troubleshoot common Windows computer, hardware, and software issues.
  • Help users with Microsoft 365 applications, including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Teams.
  • Assist with basic Adobe Acrobat tasks, including creating, combining, and editing PDFs.
  • Set up and troubleshoot laptops, monitors, docking stations, keyboards, and other peripherals.
  • Assist with printers, copiers, and scanners, and coordinate vendor service when needed.
  • Troubleshoot basic Wi-Fi, wired network, and VPN connectivity issues, escalating more complex problems to the IT team.
  • Help users with password resets and multifactor authentication using established procedures.
  • Assist with conference room equipment, video calls, and basic audiovisual setup.
  • Prepare workstations and equipment for new hires and assist with onboarding and offboarding checklists.
  • Help prepare laptops and accessories for employees traveling on business.
  • Log support requests, document troubleshooting steps, and follow up with users.
  • Maintain equipment inventory and keep IT supplies organized.
  • Follow company policies for security and handling confidential information.

Qualifications

  • 1–3 years of experience in IT support, help desk, or desktop support.
  • Working knowledge of Windows and Microsoft 365 applications.
  • Experience troubleshooting common computer, printer, and peripheral issues.
  • Basic understanding of network connectivity and VPN access.
  • Clear, patient communication and a professional, customer-focused approach.
  • Strong organization, reliability, and attention to detail.
  • Ability to follow instructions, document work, and recognize when to escalate an issue.
  • Availability to work on-site Tuesday through Thursday, full days.

Preferred

  • Experience supporting users in an office environment.
  • Familiarity with Mac computers.
  • Exposure to document management systems.
  • CompTIA A+ certification or related IT coursework.

How to Apply

Submit your resume through the recruiter managing the search.

Pay: $25 to $35 per hour

  • Embed conversational interfaces, large language models, automated decision frameworks, and smart virtual assistants directly into production systems.

  • Familiarity using API documentation and testing utilities including Swagger/OpenAPI or Postman.
  • Experience working with data processing frameworks like Talend or dbt.
  • Background working within nonprofit, education, or mission-focused environments.

job.title: SOC Cybersecurity Engineer
job.description:
Role Overview
This is a SOC (Security Operations Center) Cybersecurity Engineer. The role sits at the senior level and serves as the first escalation point above the Tier 1 analyst.
Key Responsibilities
The engineer will work across two distinct security domains: IT security (covering endpoint protection, SaaS application security, and SIEM log management) and OT (operational technology) security, which encompasses the shop floor and development team environments. Day-to-day duties include responding to and validating email phishing alerts (distinguishing false from true positives), supporting incident response escalations, and driving vulnerability management by coordinating with systems teams to remediate OS-level vulnerabilities. The role also requires communicating directly with leadership and ownership, including the ability to present and explain security issues clearly in executive settings.
Experience & Qualifications
Minimum 4–5 years of hands-on SOC engineering experience is required — not analyst experience.
Technical Environment
The organization is standardized on Rapid 7 and Palo Alto for security tooling. Candidates must have meaningful SIEM and endpoint tool experience. The company is a Microsoft shop, so familiarity with Microsoft security tools is valued; the SC-200 certification is a nice-to-have but not required and can be taught.
Compensation
Target range is $115,000–$125,000.
Work Schedule & Location
Standard hours are 8:00 AM–5:00 PM, with flexibility. The role is primarily on-site (5 days), but hybrid arrangements are open to discussion as an exception for the right candidate. After-hours on-call incidents are rare — the company has a third-party incident response partner for overnight coverage — but the engineer would be the first point of contact if escalated.

Benefits: medical, dental, vision and life insurance, a 401(k) plan and paid time off.

This role starts in New York City, where you will learn the environment, the team, the tools, and the support model. After that, the plan is for this person to relocate to Florida and become a key onsite technology resource for a growing operation.

You will support users, troubleshoot systems, help with field issues, assist with basic network administration, and become part of a team that is actively expanding.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Provide onsite field service and systems support
  • Support Windows and Mac laptops, desktops, mobile devices, printers, peripherals, and conference room technology
  • Troubleshoot hardware, software, connectivity, authentication, and access issues
  • Support Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Zoom, and collaboration tools
  • Help with basic network troubleshooting, including Wi-Fi, switch ports, access points, DHCP/DNS, and general connectivity

This is a good fit for someone who wants more than a standard support job.

You will get exposure to desktop, systems, field service, basic networking, infrastructure operations, and a growing Florida buildout. You will start by learning from an established team in NYC, then have the chance to take that knowledge with you and become an important technical resource in a new market.

If you are hands-on, sharp, reliable, and interested in relocating to Florida, this could be a really strong opportunity.
